newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Austrian, Hungarian, Slovak PMs meet for talks.
newsitem.headline: Austrian, Hungarian, Slovak PMs meet for talks.

text.p: PIESTANY, Slovakia, Nov 4 (Reuter ) - The prime ministers of Austria, Hungary and Slovakia met on Monday in the Slovak spa town of Piestany to discuss strengthening cooperation between their countries.
The talks were held to assess progress since a meeting of the three leaders last year in Austria where they agreed to expand commercial cooperation and cross-border enviromental protection.
Aides said the three leaders set out common aims in foreign policy and external and internal security matters.
After the morning session on Monday Austria's Franz Vranitzky, Hungary's Gyula Horn and Slovakia's Vladimir Meciar were due to hold bilateral talks.
However, Hungarian sources said it was unlikely that Meciar and Horn would meet. There was no immediate official comment on whether they would have bilateral talks.
Relations betwen Slovakia and Hungary are strained because of differencies over Slovakia's treatment of its 500,000-strong Hungarian minority.
Progress was achieved earlier this year, when Slovakia finaly ratified a basic treaty with Hungary.
A meeting between Meciar and Horn, scheduled in the summer, was called off after Meciar fell sick and no new date has so far been set.
